title: Generic constraints (extends) and keyof
hook: Unconstrained T can only be used where unknown works — T extends Foo unlocks Foo's members inside the generic body. keyof T extracts property names as a string union for type-safe property access.

blocks.text: A **generic constraint** limits what types can substitute for `T`: `function logLength<T extends { length: number }>(arg: T)`. Inside the function, `arg.length` is legal. **`keyof T`** produces a union of `T`'s keys: `keyof { id: string; name: string }` → `'id' | 'name'`. Combine them: `function getProp<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K]` — the return type is indexed access **T[K]**. Multiple constraints intersect: `T extends A & B`. C# uses `where T : IFoo`; TypeScript uses `T extends Foo`.

entries.plainDefinition: Upper bound on T — T must be assignable to the constraint type.
Union of string/number/symbol keys of type T.
Type of property K on T when K extends keyof T.
K limited to actual keys of T — enables safe lookup.

blocks.text: Constraints power `Pick`, `Omit`, `Record`, and every typed `get`/`set` helper. Without `extends`, you cannot call `.length`, `.compareTo`, or access properties on `T`. `keyof` + `T[K]` is the foundation of mapped types. C# interviews cover `where T : class, new()` — TS has no `new()` constraint but supports `abstract new()` patterns via constructor types. Reddit senior threads rank `keyof` + generics as essential for library authors.

blocks.title: keyof on unions
blocks.body: keyof (A | B) is keyof A & keyof B — only shared keys. keyof (A & B) is keyof A | keyof B.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Identify required members

items.body: T extends HasLength, T extends Entity, T extends keyof SomeEnum.

items.title: Use keyof for property names
items.body: K extends keyof T ties key parameter to actual properties.

items.title: Return T[K]
items.body: Indexed access preserves value type per key.

blocks.title: keyof on index signatures
blocks.body: keyof Record<string, number> includes string | number — wider than expected.

blocks.title: Over-constraining T
blocks.body: T extends object when primitives needed — use T extends string | number for unions.

blocks.text: `as const` objects give `keyof typeof CONFIG` literal keys. Conditional constraints: `T extends U ? X : never`. `keyof any` is `string | number | symbol`. For function keys, `Parameters<T>` and `ReturnType<T>` use constrained infer (module 12). No exact equivalent to C# `unmanaged` or `notnull` — use conditional types or branded types. `satisfies` validates object literals while preserving keyof inference.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot write get<T,K extends keyof T>. Confusing keyof union vs intersection. Expecting C# new() constraint in TS.

interviewTakeaways: T extends Foo — upper bound; unlocks Foo members in body.
keyof T → union of keys; T[K] → property value type.
get<T,K extends keyof T>(obj,key): T[K] — canonical safe lookup.
60s: Constraints limit generic substitution. keyof for property names. Indexed access T[K]. No runtime enforcement — erased. C# where clause is runtime-checked.
Follow-up: Pick/Omit implementation, keyof on unions, C# constraint catalog.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "extends means inheritance" — it is an upper bound for type checking.
Strong: "extends constrains T. keyof extracts keys. T[K] indexes value type. Foundation of utility types."

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS obj[key] is unchecked — TS keyof + K extends keyof T adds compile-time key validation.
C# where T : IComparable<T> mirrors T extends IComparable<T> — C# enforces at runtime, TS at compile time only.
